text:
joan: FYI customer (ACME) on Dedicated reported structured output failing intermittently. Parser error on their side when user text includes odd unicode combos and sometimes a leading BOM. Repro attached.

eva: They sent the prompt and the raw response. Their JSON parser (Rust) throws "invalid start byte" on decode.

eva: Prompt they used: "Return a JSON object with keys name and notes. notes should include the raw user text verbatim."

eva: Raw model output (base64 in ticket, decoded here):
```﻿{"name":"Jośe","notes":"Line1\nLine2"}
```

eva: You can see the output starts with a UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) and the name uses an ASCII e + combining acute (e + U+0301) instead of precomposed é. Their parser chokes at the BOM byte and then downstream code treats the combining char strangely.

joan: Customer is on Dedicated (private VPC), replica set 3 in us-west-2. They hit it in production and retried which caused duplicate billing for tokens.

michael: I reproduced locally against replica-3 by sending the same prompt in structured mode. Observed intermittent prefix_bytes=3 in the runtime traces: sometimes a 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF appears before the JSON payload. Sample log: 
``
[2026-06-01T14:22:11Z] level=info model=vicuna-13b mode=structured resp_len=123 prefix_bytes=3
```

michael: Looks like the streaming serializer sometimes writes a BOM at chunk boundary when a user input contains a leading non-printable or certain unicode normalization forms. Also noticed our tokenizer/normalization pipeline applies NFC in tokenization path but not consistently before final serialization. That can produce different byte sequences (precomposed vs combining).

ryan: Suspect a streaming/chunking bug where an earlier transformation writes a BOM to the buffer if buffer state is uninitialized. Could also be an encoding flag flipped in the C++ layer vs the Rust layer.

joan: Can we get the exact raw bytes from the customer? They attached base64: "77u/eyJuYW1lIjoiSm9zZV8xIiwi..." I decoded and confirmed leading bytes 0xEF 0xBB 0xBF.

michael: Thanks — will add a short-term server-side mitigation: strip a leading U+FEFF from structured-mode outputs before sending to customers, and enforce NFC normalization before serialization. I'll open a PR with unit tests covering a few edge cases (BOM prefix, combining chars, CRLF in notes).

jean: (typo in earlier message corrected)

joan: Customer wants to know impact to parsing, latency, and billing. They saw their client retry loop kick in after parse error which increased their token usage.

eva: I advised customer to patch their client to tolerate a leading BOM and to normalize incoming text, but emphasized we should fix server-side so it doesn't rely on client fixes.

ryan: I'll schedule a canary to strip BOM + normalize on replica-3 in us-west-2 and monitor latency. If canary looks good for 1h, roll region-wide.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: canary/release-2026-06-01 -> replica-3 (us-west-2). Started at 2026-06-01T15:03:00Z.

michael: PR opened internally: https://git.internal/redwood/serving/pulls/2345 — patch includes:
- strip leading U+FEFF for structured outputs
- run NFC normalization on final serialized strings
- tests with combining characters and BOM at chunk boundaries

joan: Will update customer with canary plan and suggested client workaround. Any idea on timeline for full rollout?

ryan: Canary duration 1 hour, then ~20 min to roll region. If no regressions, same-day rollout to other dedicated clusters. I'll monitor for any latency impact (<1% expected).

joan: Customer OK with that. Marking as escalated; will move to resolved when rollout completes and customer confirms parser no longer fails. :thumbsup:

michael: Follow-up note: also found a rare case where CRLF inside a quoted string got split across stream chunks and our JSON emitter didn't escape the split correctly — added tests for that too.

joan: Thanks all. Keeping thread open until post-rollout confirmation.
